feature: A recording leaves through the same Export sheet as everything else
summary: Saving a copy of a recording now opens the Export sheet a picture already opens, with MP4, GIF and HEIC side by side in it, the size preset beside the format instead of buried in a submenu, and two lines saying what the file will be and what it will weigh before you commit to it. It used to be a bare system save box with the format already decided by which menu item you happened to pick, and nothing said about the size.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. The flag is "A recording leaves through the same Export sheet as everything else" (next-recording-export-sheet) and it is on by default.

try.do: Open a screen recording from Capture History (⇧⌘H, then click one).
try.shotNote: Photographed while the Mac was locked. The window is the real one, drawn and driven normally, with two known costs: colours can read dimmed, and a tutorial card does not draw at all because the login window is over it.

try.do: Press ⇧⌘S. The Export sheet appears instead of a save box.
Read the two lines under Format: how big the video is and how long it runs, then what it will weigh.
Press GIF. A Quality row appears beside the format.
try.shotNote: Photographed while the Mac was locked. The window is the real one, drawn and driven normally, with two known costs: colours can read dimmed, and a tutorial card does not draw at all because the login window is over it.

try.do: Press Small, then High, and watch the line under it change size and frame rate.
Press Cancel. Nothing is written and the recording is untouched.
Trim the recording (T, drag the handles, Done), then press ⇧⌘S again and read the size line.
try.shotNote: Photographed while the Mac was locked. The window is the real one, drawn and driven normally, with two known costs: colours can read dimmed, and a tutorial card does not draw at all because the login window is over it.

try.do: Press Export…, pick a folder, and check the file that lands is the trim, not the whole clip.

evaluate: Is ⇧⌘S opening a sheet rather than a save box what you expect from a menu item called Save As, or should Save As go straight to the box and only Export… open the sheet?
Does the weight line land where your eye already is, or are you looking for it somewhere else on the sheet?
"MP4 Video · about 16 KB" on a trimmed recording: is "about" honest enough, or would you rather see no number at all than an estimate?
GIF and HEIC say "size not known until it is written" rather than guessing. Is that the right answer, or is a rough number better than none for the format you are most likely to paste into a chat?
The three formats are MP4, GIF and HEIC in one row. Is MP4 the right one for the sheet to open on?
rough: There is still no way to make an MP4 smaller. The sheet can now tell you a recording will weigh 200 MB and offers you nothing to do about it, because choosing a resolution or a bitrate is a new control the task deliberately left out. If "it is too big to send" is the thing you actually hit, this is the next piece and it needs your call on what the control should be.

A GIF and a HEIC cannot be weighed without writing them, so the sheet says so instead of guessing. Everything else about them is live: press Small and the pixel size and frame rate under it change at once.

The estimate for a re-encoded MP4 comes from what the recording itself already costs per second and per pixel. On the eight second sample it said "about 16 KB" and 16,531 bytes landed. That sample is a simple synthetic clip; a busy screen recording may drift further, and the line says "about" for that reason.

The sheet is headed Export even when you reached it through Save As. That is deliberate (saving a recording somewhere else IS the export, and there is only one sheet) but it is a wording choice worth disagreeing with.

The Mac's screen was locked for this whole run, so the keyboard and menu routes in (⇧⌘S, File ▸ Export…, Video ▸ Export…) could not be pressed: macOS freezes a background app's menu bar under a lock. They are wired and the sheet itself, every control on it and every file it writes were driven and checked for real. Pressing ⇧⌘S on an unlocked Mac is the first try step above for exactly this reason.
